title: Counter Note: The Sum Drawn to Clear a Storage Invoice
content:
The settlement is drawn for the storage accruals and the handling charges standing unpaid on the invoice named, and that total, rounded to the nearest cent, is what the member pays to clear the account. This note covers settlements on Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## The sum

1. The storage accruals standing unpaid on the invoice named are totalled.
2. The handling charges standing unpaid on the invoice named are totalled.
3. The two totals together, rounded to the nearest cent, are what the member pays.

## Order of clearing

Charges are cleared oldest first, so the settlement leaves no older charge open while clearing a later one.

## Worked sum, on hypothetical figures

An account shows storage accruals standing unpaid of 412.60 and 188.15, and handling charges standing unpaid of 96.25. The accruals come to 600.75; with the handling charges the total is 697.00; rounded to the nearest cent that is 697.00, and 697.00 is what the member pays to clear the account.

Working oldest first, the 412.60 raised in March is cleared before the 188.15 raised in April, and both before the handling charge raised in May.

## A second worked sum

An account shows a single storage accrual standing unpaid of 54.38 and no handling charges standing unpaid at all. The total drawn is 54.38, and rounded to the nearest cent that is 54.38.

## Points of judgement

**Charges already settled.** Only what stands unpaid is drawn into the sum; a charge already cleared is not drawn in again.

**A part payment.** Because the oldest charges are cleared first, a payment smaller than the total drawn clears the earliest charges and leaves the later ones standing, rather than the other way about.
